title: Widen writer flush batch to 512 (4MB) on accepted commit_delay=0/commit_siblings=20 base
configuration_cause: wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) still leaves wal_waiting_backends p95=1 and sync_average_ms=0.112ms; the accepted r014 bundle proved removing the fixed commit_delay stall is the dominant win, but the writer-side flush batch was never pushed past 256 within the same accepted base.
mechanism: r014 accepted commit_delay=0, commit_siblings=20, wal_writer_flush_after=256 with +16-24% TPS and InsertTweet p95 down 15-33%. The remaining wal_wait anomaly (p95=1 backend, sync 0.112ms) is now writer-side, not commit-side: with commit_delay=0 there is no foreground sleep, so the only lever left in the bundle is the background writer flush batch. Doubling wal_writer_flush_after 256->512 (4MB) coalesces more WAL writes per fsync without adding any per-commit latency, since commit_siblings=20 keeps the group-commit window inactive. This is a larger safe amplitude of the same supported mechanism, not a new direction.
query_effect: No plan change expected; GetUserTweets path untouched. InsertTweet commit path benefits from fewer writer fsyncs.
expected_tps_effect: Small positive: +0.3-1.5% successful_transaction_tps versus incumbent 36506 rps, driven by reduced writer-side WAL queueing.

predictions.rationale: Larger writer flush batch (4MB vs 2MB) coalesces more writes per fsync, lowering mean sync time.
Fewer writer fsyncs reduce backends waiting on WAL flush.
Freed terminal capacity from shorter commit path raises completed TPS.

alternatives.statement: If 2MB already saturates the writer flush batching, doubling to 4MB yields no measurable sync-time change and TPS stays flat.
If the residual wal_wait is commit-side rather than writer-side, reintroducing a small commit_delay would help; but r005-r010 refuted that direction, so we predict it stays refuted.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Keeps the accepted r014 base (commit_delay=0, commit_siblings=20) and pushes the only remaining actionable writer-side knob to a larger safe amplitude (512 vs 256), targeting the still-active wal_wait anomaly without reintroducing any per-commit stall.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Double from incumbent 256 to 512 (8kB units = 4MB), inside allowed [0,1024]; larger safe amplitude of the r014-supported writer-side flush batching mechanism.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; coalesces background WAL writes into fewer fsyncs

nodes.label: Larger writer flush batch coalesces WAL writes into fewer fsyncs
